chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn [Yahya] from Ahmad and Abdullah, sons of Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
a man who marries a woman and stipulates for her that he will not take her out of her country, he said: 'He fulfills that for her' or he said: 'That is binding upon him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a husband's promise not to move his wife from her hometown in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the stipulation of 'non-relocation' (al-istiqrar) as a binding contractual condition (shart) within the marriage contract, reflecting the Shia principle that conditions agreed upon by the spouses are valid unless they contradict the essence of marriage. This ruling underscores the legal autonomy of the wife to secure her social and familial stability, ensuring the husband's adherence to the agreed terms as a matter of legal obligation (lazam).
